thread:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for service=model-serving image=redwood/model-serving:v1.4.2  — 10% traffic -> canary group A. Trigger: automated-release pipeline #4821

amanda: @oncall-kate paging — we're seeing a spike in 5xxs from canary (customers hitting streaming endpoints). triage-bot alerted on p50/p95 jump.

oncall-kate: on it. joining incident channel. can you drop the first lines of logs?

amanda: logs pasted below (redacted keys). main error: repeated websocket timeouts and OOM eviction traces on node gpu-23
```
ERROR 16:32:10 upstream/connect timeout id=abc123 session=... websocket: write tcp 10.1.3.22:443: write: connection reset by peer
kubelet: eviction manager: memory available below eviction threshold on node gpu-23
```

raj: rolling latency + client side timeouts. Some customers reported aborted streams. We saw 2.3% error rate on canary vs 0.1% baseline.

sasha: @amanda which change is new in v1.4.2? any kernel/rpc change?

amanda: mostly batching kernel change + a change that toggles aggressive kv-cache prefetch; also a new feature-flag "prefetch_workload" enabled by default for canary.

triage-bot: Incident severity: SEV3 -> elevated. Pager routed to oncall-kate and infra.

oncall-kate: quick plan: 1) check if auto-rollback kicked 2) if not, try manual rollback / flag flip 3) run smoke tests 4) if stable, scale canary back to 0%.

amanda: auto-rollback is configured but only if `slo.breach=true` in rollout policy. I don't see an automated trigger in the deploy logs — maybe the metric window didn't exceed threshold.

infra-bot: Alert: node gpu-23 reports memory pressure and restarted nvidia-container-runtime at 16:31:45. Pod restarts on that node: model-serving-canary-5, model-serving-canary-3.

raj: we should not evict the entire canary yet. if it's a prefetch bug we can flip the feature flag to disable prefetch without a full rollback — that will be faster. but flag is behind "reclaim_mode" gating which is currently stuck OFF due to a config propagation issue.

oncall-kate: I can set the feature flag via the admin console. running: `redwood-ffctl set prefetch_workload false --env prod --scope canary-group-a`

amanda: command accepted but flag state did not converge — agent reports "target unreachable" for canary group A.

oncall-kate: trying alternate: `kubectl -n prod exec deploy/model-serving-canary-5 -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/flags/reset?prefetch=false`

sasha: heads up — that pod is on gpu-23 (the one with mem pressure). executing on a different canary pod.

oncall-kate: executed on model-serving-canary-3. response: 200 OK, {"prefetch_workload":"disabled"}

amanda: good. flipping traffic to canary=0% in the router as a precaution: `routerctl set-weight model-serving 0 --subset canary-group-a`

deploy-bot: Traffic shift executed: canary-group-a -> 0% at 16:33:12 by oncall-kate (operator: routerctl).

pm-lin: any visible customer impact? which customers/SLAs hit timeouts?

raj: partial: 12 streaming sessions aborted (mostly internal beta partners), payment engine retries caught most work. No broad data loss. Some increased tail latency for a small set of tenants who hit the canary endpoints directly.

triage-bot: Creating incident doc -> https://redwood-ops/incidents/1976543210 (auto).

oncall-kate: running smoke test now: `bash ./tools/smoke/run_stream_test.sh --target model-serving.prod.redwood.ai`

amanda: smoke script now passing 5/5 streams stable on control and 5/5 on remaining prod instances. p95 back to baseline.

raj: recommend we keep canary at 0% and mark this as manual safety-net activation. I'll start a manual rollback of the canary deployment to v1.4.1 to ensure the environment is clean. command: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/model-serving-canary --to-revision=17`

oncall-kate: please hold on rollback until I confirm no further OOMs on nodes. infra team is cleaning GPU node, draining and rebooting gpu-23.

infra-bot: Node gpu-23 cordoned and drained at 16:35:40. Reboot scheduled.

raj: ack — pausing rollback. we'll keep the flag disabled and traffic at 0%.

sasha: after reboot, we should run targeted load tests with prefetch disabled and track CPU/GPU utilization to see if the batching kernel caused mem spike.

oncall-kate: accepted. handing off to infra for next 90m for root cause analysis. @infra oncall please take postmortem.

infra-bot: Assigned: @sasha (infra) to investigate node-level memory regression and container runtime restarts.

pm-lin: customer comms: tier-2 notified. no external status update needed yet, but keep the comms team in loop.

amanda: adding note: feature flag propagation failed for the group initially because the config agent was rate-limited by the control plane during a deployment surge. we've queued a follow-up to increase agent retry backoff.

oncall-kate: summary we will share in incident doc: 1) Canary v1.4.2 introduced prefetech + new batching kernel 2) Node gpu-23 memory pressure led to pod restarts and websocket timeouts 3) Auto-rollback did not trigger (metric window/misconfig) 4) We manually disabled prefetch flag, shifted canary to 0%, cordoned/rebooted node, and are holding manual rollback pending infra verification 5) Impact: limited aborted streams for small set of customers, no data loss.

raj: i'll follow up to schedule a patch: either revert v1.4.2 -> v1.4.1 or cut v1.4.3 with prefetch disabled and a safer caching profile.

pm-lin: thanks everyone. oncall-kate, please handoff when you finish the verification checks. :thumbsup:

oncall-kate: handing off to @sasha at 17:05 UTC for RCA. closing live mitigation channel. If any regressions show up, page immediately. :white_check_mark:

triage-bot: Incident status: mitigation in place. severity downgraded to MONITORING.

sasha: taking ownership of RCA, will coordinate with runtime team about kernel/batching interaction.

amanda: creating follow-up ticket to add automated-rollback coverage for streaming websocket errors and to harden flag propagation.

--- end of thread ---
